title: Python Essentials: Exceptions, Collections, pathlib, json, Typing & the GIL
summary: Quick revision notes on Python error handling (try/except/else/finally, custom exceptions, raising), the collections helpers Counter, defaultdict and deque, pathlib, json, basic type hints, and what the GIL does and does not do.

chapters.title: Exception Handling Mental Model
points: An exception is an object raised at runtime that unwinds the call stack until a matching except clause catches it; uncaught, it ends the program with a traceback
try/except/else/finally order: else runs only if try raised nothing; finally always runs, even after return, break or an uncaught exception
except clauses are checked top to bottom and the first match wins, so list specific subclasses before parents like Exception
Catch several types with a tuple: except (KeyError, IndexError) as e; e is deleted when the except block ends
Mistake: bare except: or except BaseException swallows KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit; catch Exception at most, and a specific type by default

chapters.title: Raising and Custom Exceptions
points: raise ValueError('msg') raises a new exception; a bare raise inside an except block re-raises the current one with its traceback intact
raise NewError() from err sets __cause__ (explicit chaining); raising inside an except block without from sets __context__ automatically; from None suppresses the chain
Custom exception: class AppError(Exception): pass; subclass Exception, never BaseException; give a base class per library and subclass it for specific cases
Add context by overriding __init__ and storing fields (e.g. self.code) and calling super().__init__(msg); callers read e.args and the attributes
Mistake: except Exception: pass hides bugs, and raising a bare string or catching only to print and continue loses the failure; log or re-raise instead

chapters.title: Collections: Counter, defaultdict, deque
points: Counter(iterable) counts hashables; .most_common(n) returns the top n (item, count) pairs, missing keys give 0 instead of KeyError, and counters support + and - arithmetic
defaultdict(list) calls the factory to create a missing value on first access: d[k].append(x) needs no key check; factory can be int, list, set or a lambda
Mistake: reading a missing key in a defaultdict inserts it; use d.get(k) or k in d to test without side effects
deque(maxlen=n) is a double-ended queue with O(1) append, appendleft, pop and popleft; a full maxlen deque drops items from the opposite end
deque vs list: list.pop(0) and insert(0, x) are O(n), so use deque for queues; deque indexing in the middle is O(n)

chapters.title: pathlib and json
points: Path('data') / 'file.txt' joins paths with the / operator; use Path.cwd(), Path.home(), .parent, .name, .stem and .suffix instead of string slicing
p.read_text(encoding='utf-8') and p.write_text(s) read or write whole files; p.exists(), p.is_file(), p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) and p.glob('*.py') cover everyday filesystem work
json.dumps(obj, indent=2) and json.loads(s) convert to and from strings; json.dump(obj, f) and json.load(f) work on file objects (the s means string)
JSON maps dict to object, list and tuple to array, None to null, True to true; tuples come back as lists and dict keys become strings
Mistake: json.dumps fails with TypeError on datetime, set or custom objects; pass default=str or a custom function, and open json files with explicit utf-8 encoding

chapters.title: Typing Basics and the GIL
points: Type hints annotate only: def f(x: int, y: str = 'a') -> bool; Python does not enforce them at runtime, tools like mypy and pyright check them
Common forms: list[int], dict[str, int], tuple[int, ...], int | None (or Optional[int]), Callable[[int], str] and Any as an escape hatch

The GIL lets only one thread execute Python bytecode at a time in the default CPython build, so CPU-bound threads gain no speedup (the free-threaded build, e.g. python3.14t, has no GIL and runs threads in parallel)
Threads still help for I/O-bound work because the GIL is released while waiting on I/O; use multiprocessing or ProcessPoolExecutor for CPU-bound parallelism
Mistake: assuming the GIL makes code thread-safe, since compound operations like counter += 1 are not atomic; protect shared state with threading.Lock

chapters.title: Python Essentials Cheat Sheet
points: try/except/else/finally: else runs on success, finally always; order except clauses specific to general; bare raise re-raises, raise X from e chains
Custom errors: class AppError(Exception); catch Exception not BaseException; never except: pass
Counter.most_common(n), defaultdict(list), deque(maxlen=n) with O(1) appendleft/popleft
Path('a') / 'b', read_text, write_text, mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True), glob; json dumps/loads for strings, dump/load for files
Hints are unenforced (int | None, list[int]); GIL means threads for I/O, processes for CPU, and Lock for shared state
